clue.text: Estimate king is held by our next-door neighbour at 27

parts.note: a quotation is a builder's estimate of a price

indicators.note: something held by another sits inside it, so the king letter goes into the planet

parts.note: Mars is the planet next to Earth, our neighbour in the solar system
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A guess about a king being kept captive by the people living next door at number 27.
explanation.walkthrough: '27' is the cross-reference: the answer means the same as 27-across, the punctuation enclosing speech; 'at' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Quotation marks and inverted commas are two names for the same punctuation around quoted speech.

clue.text: Trained musket on Iraq?

indicators.note: a gun trained on a target is aimed, but here trained means the letters are drilled into a new order

explanation.surface: Was a gun aimed at Iraq? The clue asks the question itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: it ends with the very punctuation the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue closes on a punctuation sign of query, which is exactly what the answer names.

clue.text: Helpful having fluorine in the water

indicators.note: the river has the element symbol in it, so one goes inside the other
the river has the element symbol in it, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: the Ouse is an English river, a body of water
F is the chemical symbol for fluorine

explanation.surface: Fluoride in drinking water is beneficial.
explanation.walkthrough: The OUSE is a river in Yorkshire (and another in Sussex).
explanation.definitionFit: Being of use is an idiom meaning serviceable or helpful.

clue.text: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John in such a girlie group? No 19 for them!

definitions.text: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John in such a girlie group? No 19 for them!

parts.words: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John in such a girlie group? No 19 for them!
parts.note: the four gospel writers are all canonised, and a famous 1990s British girl band shares the name; saints commit no wrongdoing, the answer to 19

explanation.surface: Imagining the four evangelists in a pop girl band, and noting they never do wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: All Saints were a British girl band of the late 1990s; 19-down is MISDEED, which saints do not commit.
explanation.definitionFit: The evangelists are all saints, and the girl group's name is the same phrase.

clue.text: Undies off during sex? On the contrary, if so "mashed"

indicators.note: during means the sex letter sits within the other piece
this flips the order the clue states, so the scrambled underwear surrounds the sex letter instead
off says the letters of the underwear word are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: F stands for female, one of the two sexes

explanation.surface: A racy scene where underwear comes off during sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undies off during sex' would put the anagram of UNDIES inside F; 'On the contrary' reverses that, so F goes into the anagram. 'if so' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In northern England tea is mashed when it is brewed, that is, steeped or infused in hot water.

clue.text: "0-0 at half-time" sent in radio report from the Riverside?

parts.note: a zero can be read as nil
the second zero is read as the letter O

indicators.note: half says keep only the front half of the word that follows it in the clue

parts.note: said over the radio, sent sounds like cent, and C is the abbreviation for cent

explanation.surface: A goalless score at the interval being broadcast on the radio from a ground called the Riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riverside is Middlesbrough's football ground; the definition plays on 'from the river', the Nile. 'at' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Nilotic means relating to the Nile, so of or from that river's side.

clue.text: Mayo man is oil rig's regular visitor

indicators.note: regular says take letters at a steady interval, every second one of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A man from County Mayo often visits an oil platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mayo' looks like the Irish county; it is short for mayonnaise. 'visitor' rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a garlic mayonnaise, so it is a kind of mayo.

clue.text: Learning king's currently on left side

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
now means at present, currently
an edge is a side or border

explanation.surface: Studying how the monarch currently sits on the left side.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge is what one acquires by learning, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Peer lacking some noble qualities

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lord who lacks the nobility his title suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Peer lacking' as the definition, but 'lacking' is a link word; 'Peer' alone means an equal.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is someone of equal standing, a person on the same level.

clue.text: Continue straight after dog-leg

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A golfer's instruction to keep going straight once past the dog-leg on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a team made to follow on must bat again straight after its first innings.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the follow-on means a side batting again immediately after its first innings.

clue.text: Can a mole exist with its head cut off? No! Never!

annotationWithheld.why: Can a mole exist with its head cut off? No! Never! (12): CAN A MOLE + (E)XIST rearranges to the answer, but no clue word signals the anagram, so the parse cannot be written honestly.
annotationWithheld.clue: Can a mole exist with its head cut off? No! Never!

clue.text: Low life of digital newspapers?

parts.note: a toe is a digit of the foot
rags is slang for poor-quality newspapers

explanation.surface: The seedy side of online newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital' looks like online media; it means a digit, here of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Toerags is British slang for contemptible people, lowlifes.

clue.text: See-through material that's branded XXX

definitions.meaning: a brand of toughened laminated glass
three crosses is a threefold X, as on strong ale or adult films

explanation.surface: A transparent product marked with three crosses.
explanation.definitionFit: Triplex is a trademark laminated safety glass, and triple-X reads as the three-cross marking.

clue.text: Something played by men on horseback

parts.note: OR is short for other ranks, soldiers rather than officers

indicators.note: the back half of horseback signals that the horse word is read in reverse

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: Polo or some sport played by riders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horseback' splits into 'horse' and 'back', the reversal signal; 'by' and 'on' link.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a musical instrument, something that is played.

clue.text: Envying endlessly randy rookie?

parts.note: green means envious, as in green with envy

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: horny is slang for randy

explanation.surface: A lustful novice consumed with jealousy.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenhorn is an inexperienced newcomer, a novice or beginner.

clue.text: Like crabs and lobsters with a shell covered by transfer design

indicators.note: covered by means the inner pieces sit inside the transfer word

parts.note: a decal is a design printed for transfer onto a surface
a pod is the shell or husk of a seed such as a pea

explanation.surface: Crustaceans whose shells are decorated with a transfer pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs and lobsters belong to the ten-footed crustacean order, so they are described by this adjective.

clue.text: Playing polo with a very informal Frenchman

indicators.note: playing means the letters of the fodder are moved about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone playing polo alongside a very relaxed man from France.
explanation.walkthrough: Parleyvoo, from 'parlez-vous', is jocular British slang for a Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Parleyvoo is a slangy, informal word for a French person, from French speech.

clue.text: Big Eddy has drunk more malts

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Big Eddy has had too much whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big Eddy' looks like a person; an eddy is a whirl of water. 'has' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool, a very large eddy.

clue.text: Muscle in repose, I admire you!

indicators.note: in places the muscle word inside the word for repose

parts.note: rest means repose
a pec is a pectoral muscle

explanation.surface: Admiring someone's toned muscles as they relax.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Respect!' is a slang exclamation expressing admiration for someone.

clue.text: This did seem wrong?

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are set out incorrectly, in a new order

explanation.surface: Something seemed to be wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' points to the answer itself: a wrongful act would indeed seem wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A misdeed is a wrongful act, which naturally seems wrong.

clue.text: Bodily emission initially recurring hourly, ending up monthly

indicators.note: initially says take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A discharge that comes back every hour, eventually once a month.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a watery discharge from the eyes or nose, a bodily secretion.

clue.text: Deciding races are fun for about half of us

indicators.note: about means the letters are turned around and rearranged
half of takes one letter of the two-letter word, here its second half

explanation.surface: Races that are fun for roughly half of the people.
explanation.definitionFit: Run-offs are extra contests held to decide a tie, deciding races.

clue.text: Piece of film portraying some terrific heroism

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A movie scene showing great bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Piece of film portraying' as the definition, but 'portraying' is a link word; 'Piece of film' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiche is a sheet of microfilm, a piece of film holding miniature pages.

clue.text: Fix return of best pan

parts.note: a stew is a fix, a predicament

indicators.note: return of means the word for best is read backwards

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks

explanation.surface: Repairing the return of the best pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A stewpot is a deep cooking pot, a kind of pan.

clue.text: Edge found after turning up for the festival

indicators.note: found after places the edge word behind the flipped piece
turning means the little word is flipped back to front

parts.note: a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: An edge discovered after something turned up for the festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Purim is a Jewish festival commemorating Esther's saving of the Jews in Persia.

clue.text: Setter from Tory Island

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, a Tory
Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: A crossword setter from Tory Island off Donegal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler; it means something that sets hard. Tory Island is a real island off Ireland, misleading. 'from' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete is a building material that sets hard, so it is a setter.

clue.text: Ill-tempered woman with no ace to follow king? That's a sign

definitions.text: to follow king? That's a sign

indicators.note: with no says the letter for ace is taken out

parts.note: a virago is a bad-tempered, domineering woman
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A grumpy woman with no ace left to play after the king in a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'king' is Leo, the lion, king of beasts: the zodiac sign coming after Leo is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgo is the zodiac sign that follows Leo, the lion being king of the beasts.

clue.text: Varied comments after moving introduction to speech?

indicators.note: after moving means the letters of the fodder are shifted around into a new order

explanation.surface: Different remarks given once an opening speech has been shifted.
explanation.walkthrough: Opening punctuation marks introduce direct speech, hence the definition with its question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverted commas open a passage of quoted speech, so they introduce it.
